title: IMO Casualty Investigation Code as international marine safety-investigation rail
summary: The IMO Casualty Investigation Code is encoded as an international safety-investigation rail: it supports objective marine safety investigations, separates safety purpose from legal proceedings without suppressing causal-factor reporting, and provides evidence-access/reopening concepts.

status_history.note: Added as rev0028 marine casualty investigation / correction rail.

place.scope: marine casualty investigation and safety-learning infrastructure

subjects.name: IMO Casualty Investigation Code as international marine safety-investigation rail

claims.claim: IMO says it adopted MSC.255(84), the Casualty Investigation Code, and SOLAS amendments make parts I and II mandatory.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The Code is framed to facilitate objective marine safety investigations for future safety and does not preclude civil, criminal or administrative proceedings or full reporting on causal factors even if blame/liability can be inferred.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The Code also supports investigation independence, evidence access including recorded data/VDRs, and reopening when new evidence materially alters conclusions.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

type_payload.signal_capture_model: code framework for marine safety investigations, evidence access, independence and reporting of causal factors
limitations: code adoption does not prove national implementation quality
investigation independence and evidence access can vary
legal proceedings and safety investigation may interact differently by jurisdiction

handling_notes: Infrastructure records are correction-memory surfaces, not guarantees that recommendations or operating practice actually changed.
Marine-casualty records must preserve the dignity of passengers, crew, families, responders, and survivors.
Do not collapse safety-investigation causal language into individual blame; separate safety investigation, legal liability, vessel operation, design, maintenance, and emergency-response surfaces.
This is historical/evidentiary infrastructure, not operational navigation, stability, damage-control, legal, regulatory, or emergency guidance.

next_actions: Create child records for SOLAS/ro-ro regulation changes and Casualty Investigation Code implementation examples.
